Rashi on Ketubot 44b:11:1.hebrew: אלא כאן נערה כו' - אלא האי דכתיב מלא, לא ללמד על עצמו בא ולהוציא את הקטנה — דבלאו הך דרשא אמעיטא לה קטנה, כדאמרינן, דלאו בת עונשין — אלא ללמד בא על כל נערה שבתורה שכתובין חסר, לומר שאף הקטנה במשמע. והכי יליף: כאן נערה — כאן שאי אפשר בקטנה כתיב מלא, הא למדת שכל מקום שנכתב חסר, אף הקטנה במשמע, כגון באונס ומפתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 44b:11:1.english: Rather, here [it is written] na’ara, etc. - Rather, this [instance] that is written in full [with a heh] did not come to teach about itself and exclude a minor — for without this exposition a minor is [already] excluded, as we said, because she is not subject to punishment — rather, it came to teach about all [instances of] na’ara in the Torah that are written defectively [without a heh], to say that even a minor is included in the meaning. And this is how it derives [it]: Here [it says] na’ara — here, where it is impossible [to refer] to a minor, it is written in full; thus you learn that wherever it is written defectively, even a minor is included in the meaning, such as in [the cases of] a rapist and a seducer.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:12:1.english: Three rules - regarding the execution of a betrothed young woman.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:12:2.english: Witnesses came [to testify] about her in her father-in-law's house - After she was married.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:12:3.english: That she committed adultery in her father's house - [That is,] during betrothal.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:1:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - That [one whose] conception was not in sanctity and [whose] birth was in sanctity [is executed] by stoning.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:1:2.hebrew: ומתה - ״וסקלוה כל אנשי עירה באבנים ומתה״, והאי ״ומתה״ קרא יתירא הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 44b:1:2.english: And she shall die - "And all the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die," and this [phrase] "and she shall die" is a superfluous verse.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:3:1.english: In Israel - [As the verse states:] “For she has committed a vile deed in Israel.”

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:5:1.hebrew: מאן ימאן - במפתה הכתוב מדבר, דמצי למיכתב "ואם ימאן", וכתב "ואם מאן ימאן" — בין אביה קיים וממאן, בין שאין אביה קיים והיא ממאנת. אלמא, אע"ג דכתיב באונס "ונתן לאבי הנערה" [שם], ואונס ומפתה מהדדי גמירי, מיחייב קנס איתומה. וכי תימא: שאני הכא דרבי רחמנא [אבל לגבי מוציא ש"ר לא אתרבאי] — הכא נמי לאו יתומה משמע מריבוי, אלא דבין היא ובין אביה יכולין לעכב, כדאמרינן באלו נערות (לעיל כתובות דף לט:), ויתומה לא אתרבאי הכא; אלא דסבירא ליה לתנא ד"אביה" דקאמר קרא לאו למעוטי יתומה, אלא למימרא דקנסה לאביה ולא לעצמה, והוא הדין ל"אביה" האמור במוציא שם רע [דברים כב]:
Rashi on Ketubot 44b:5:1.english: Utterly refuse - Scripture is speaking of a seducer, for it could have written "if he refuse," yet it wrote "if he utterly refuse" — whether her father is alive and he refuses, or whether her father is not alive and she refuses. Thus, even though it is written regarding a rapist, "and he shall give to the father of the young woman" (ibid.), and [the laws of] a rapist and a seducer are derived from one another, he is liable for the fine for an orphan. And if you say: It is different here because the Merciful One included [her], whereas regarding a defamer [motzi shem ra] she was not included — here too, an orphan is not implied from the amplification; rather, [it teaches] that both she and her father can prevent [the marriage], as we say in [the chapter] Eilu Ne'arot (above, Ketubot 39b), and an orphan was not included here. Rather, the Tanna holds that "her father" which the verse states is not [meant] to exclude an orphan, but rather to say that her fine belongs to her father and not to herself; and the same law applies to "her father" stated regarding a defamer (Deuteronomy 22).

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:6:1.english: He raises the objection, etc. - [Regarding] this orphan that the Tanna mentioned:

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:6:2.hebrew: בבא עליה ואח"כ נתיתמה - ולעולם אבי הנערה למעוטי יתומה, בין בקנס בין בהוצאת שם רע:
Rashi on Ketubot 44b:6:2.english: [It refers to one] who had relations with her and afterward she was orphaned - And in all cases, [the verse] "the father of the young woman" [serves] to exclude an orphan, whether regarding a fine or regarding defamation.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:7:1.english: Rava said [he is] liable - One who defames an orphan.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:7:2.hebrew: מדתני אמי כי הוציא שם רע על בתולת ישראל ולא בתולת גרים - והא בתולת גרים יתומה היא, דרחמנא אפקריה לזרעיה דמצרי כשל חמור, דכתיב (יחזקאל כ״ג:כ׳) "וזרמת סוסים זרמתם", והוא לשון שכבת זרע הזורם כזרם מים, ואצטריך קרא למעוטי. אי אמרת בשלמא כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 44b:7:2.english: From [the fact] that Ami taught: "Because he brought an evil name upon a virgin of Israel" — and not a virgin of converts - Now, a virgin convert is [like] an orphan, for the Merciful One declared the seed of an Egyptian [i.e., a non-Jew] ownerless like that of a donkey, as it is written (Ezekiel 23:20): "and the issue of horses is their issue," and it is an expression of semen that flows like a stream of water — and yet a verse was needed to exclude [her]. Granted, if you say, etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 44b:9:1.hebrew: נערה מלא דבר הכתוב - בכל מקום כתיב נער, וכאן כתיב נערה מלא, להוציא את הקטנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 44b:9:1.english: Na’arah [written] in full, the verse spoke - Everywhere [else] it is written na’ar, and here it is written na’arah in full, to exclude a minor.

Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:10:1.hebrew: הא לאו הכי ה"א אפילו קטנה והכתיב ואם אמת היה - נראה לר"י, דלא בעי רב אחא למילף קנס ממיתה, דכל היכא דלא מחייב מיתה לא מחייב קנס, ולא בעי למימר נמי: הואיל וקרא איירי בגדולה, כל דינין שבפרשה אין נוהגין אלא בגדולה. אלא הכי פריך: טעמא דכתב רחמנא "נערה" בה"א, הא לאו הכי ה"א אפילו קטנה במשמע — והיינו משום דכיון דלא כתיב ה"א ביטל משמעות נערה, דמשמע דווקא גדולה — והא כתיב: "אם אמת וגו'", וקטנה לאו בת עונשין היא, ואפ"ה כתב "נערה" חסר! אלמא משום חסרון ה"א אינו מבוטל משמעות נערה, דהוי גדולה. והשתא לא קשה מידי לרבנן מנא להו דמחייבי סקילה בבא על הקטנה, והא קרא בבת עונשין איירי — דהא הכא לא בעי למעוטי קטנה מקנס משום דקרא בבת עונשין איירי, אלא כדפרישית. ולא תקשי נמי אמאי איצטריך "בתולת ישראל", תיפוק ליה מ"בישראל" דגבי סקילה, דהא לא ילפינן מהדדי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:10:1.english: "If that were not so, I would say even a minor [is included]; isn't it written: 'But if [this matter] is true...'" - It appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that Rav Aḥa does not mean to derive [the law of] the fine from [the law of] the death penalty — [to claim] that wherever one is not liable to the death penalty, one is not liable to the fine — nor does he mean to say that since the verse speaks of an adult, all laws in the passage apply only to an adult. Rather, this is what he is asking: [You claim that] the reason [a minor is excluded] is that the Merciful One wrote na'arah with a hei, whereas if not for that, I would have thought even a minor is implied — which is because once the hei is not written, it nullifies the [ordinary] meaning of na'arah, which implies specifically an adult — but isn't it written: "If [this matter] is true..." etc., and a minor is not eligible for punishment, and yet [the Torah] wrote na'arah defectively [without a hei]! Thus, due to the omission of the hei, the meaning of na'arah — namely, that she is an adult — is not nullified. And now there is no difficulty at all [with the question]: according to the Rabbis, from where do they derive that they obligate stoning for one who cohabits with a minor, given that the verse speaks of one eligible for punishment — for here [Rav Aḥa] does not seek to exclude a minor from the fine on the grounds that the verse speaks of one eligible for punishment, rather [he argues] as I have explained. And furthermore, it is not difficult why "a virgin of Israel" is needed — [why not] derive it from "in Israel" [written] regarding stoning — because we do not derive them from one another.

Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:12:1.hebrew: הא כל מקום שנאמר נער אפי' קטנה במשמע - ור"מ נמי הוה דריש הכי, אי לאו משום ד"לו תהיה לאשה" דדריש לעיל (כתובות דף מ:) במהוה עצמה. וא"ת: הואיל ומסתבר למדרש דכל מקום שנאמר נער אפילו קטנה במשמע כרבנן, נימא לר"מ דווקא באונס ומפתה דגלי קרא גלי, אבל בכל מקום נדרוש דאפילו קטנה במשמע? ואור"י דהיינו טעמא דר"מ: דאי דווקא לאונס ומפתה אתא קרא ד"ולו תהיה לאשה", ליכתוב בהו "נערה" מלא כמו במוציא שם רע, וה"א: כאן "נערה", הא בכל מקום כו'; ומדכתיב "לו תהיה לאשה" במהוה עצמה, בא ללמד דבכל מקום שנאמר נער — כמו הכא, במהוה עצמה מיירי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:12:1.english: Thus, wherever it is stated na'ar, even a minor is indicated - And Rabbi Meir would also have expounded [it] this way, were it not for [the verse] "she shall be his wife" (Deuteronomy 22:29), which he expounds above (Ketubot 40b) as [referring to] one who can confer herself [in marriage]. And if you ask: Since it is logical to expound that wherever na'ar is stated, even a minor is indicated, like the Rabbis [do], let us say according to Rabbi Meir [that] specifically in [the cases of] a rapist and a seducer, where the verse revealed [this], it revealed [it], but everywhere [else] let us expound that even a minor is indicated! And Ri explains that this is Rabbi Meir's reason: For if the verse "and she shall be his wife" came specifically for a rapist and a seducer, it should have written na'arah in full in them, just as in [the case of] a defamer, and I would have said: Here [it writes] na'arah, thus everywhere [else it means even a minor, etc.]. Rather, from the fact that it is written "she shall be his wife" — [referring to] one who can confer herself [in marriage] — it comes to teach that wherever na'ar is stated, just like here, it is speaking of one who can confer herself [in marriage].

Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:1:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - Because it is written "in Israel," [the Gemara] asks [this].

Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:2:1.hebrew: ואימא לרבות הורתה ולידתה בקדושה? ההיא ישראלית מעלייתא היא - תימה: דגבי חליצה, דדרשינן (יבמות דף קב.) מ"ונקרא שמו בישראל" דאין כשר לדין חליצה עד שיהא אביו ואמו מישראל — אלמא ממעטי מ"בישראל" אפי' הורתו ולידתו בקדושה! וכ"ת דהתם, משום דהורתו שלא בקדושה לא אצטריך למעוטי, ד"מקרב אחיך" ידעינן בכל דין דבעינן הורתו ולידתו בקדושה, ואייתר גבי דין חליצה "בישראל" עד שיהא אביו ואמו מישראל — אכתי איכא לאקשויי: אימא ד"בישראל" אתא למעוטי הורתו שלא בקדושה אפי' לחליצת בני גרים, ד"מקרב אחיך" לא דרשינן אלא למיפסליה לדין ישראל, אבל גר חבירו מצי דיין, כדדרשינן התם: "עליך" הוא דבעינן "מקרב אחיך" כו'. ואור"י: כיון דהורתו ולידתו בקדושה, ישראל מעליא הוא, כדאמרינן הכא. אם כן, הכי נמי בני גרים, כיון שהורתן ולידתן בקדושה, הוו ישראל מעלייתא, וקרינא בהו "עליך". והואיל וכן, בלא "ונקרא שמו בישראל" נפקא לן שפסול גר לחליצת בני גרים, דבעינן "מקרב אחיך" — עד שתהא אמו מישראל; ולהכי אייתר "בישראל" לאצרוכי אביו מישראל:
Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:2:1.english: Say [that this verse comes] to include [a girl whose] conception and birth were in sanctity? That [girl] is a full-fledged Jewish woman - [This is] astonishing: for regarding chalitzah, where we expound (Yevamot 102a) from "and his name shall be called in Israel" that [a convert] is not qualified to judge chalitzah unless both his father and his mother are from Israel — thus, they exclude from "in Israel" even one whose conception and birth were in sanctity! And if you will say that there [in the case of chalitzah], [the verse] did not need to exclude one whose conception was not in sanctity, because from "from among your brethren" we know regarding every judgment that we require his conception and birth to be in sanctity, and therefore "in Israel" was left superfluous regarding the law of chalitzah [to teach that he is disqualified] until both his father and his mother are from Israel — still there is [room] to object: Say that "in Israel" comes to exclude one whose conception was not in sanctity even for the chalitzah of the children of converts, for "from among your brethren" we expound only to disqualify him for judging a [born] Jew, whereas he may judge his fellow convert, as we expound there: It is "over you" that we require "from among your brethren," etc. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: Since his conception and birth were in sanctity, he is a full-fledged Jew, as we say here. If so, so too the children of converts: since their conception and birth were in sanctity, they are full-fledged Jews, and we apply to them "over you." And since this is so, even without "and his name shall be called in Israel," we derive that a convert is disqualified for the chalitzah of the children of converts, because we require "from among your brethren" — [meaning] until his mother is from Israel; and therefore "in Israel" was left superfluous to require [that] his father [also be] from Israel:

Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:3:1.hebrew: אם כן בישראל מאי אהני ליה - תימה לרשב"א, דנימא אהני ליה שלא ילקה ולא ישלם מאה כסף! ואור"י, דסברא הוא שיהנה לכל הכתוב בפרשה. ועוד אור"י, דלענין מלקות ומאה כסף לא איצטריך למעוטי מ"בישראל", דמ"בתולת ישראל" — ולא בתולת גרים — ממעטינן להו. והשתא אתי שפיר, דלא תיקשי: אמאי איצטריך "בתולת ישראל" — ולא בתולת גרים? תיפוק ליה מ"בישראל"! ואע"ג דלגבי מיתה כתיב, מ"מ גמרינן מינה קנס, כדמשמע בסמוך, דקאמר: טעמא דכתב רחמנא "נערה", הא לאו הכי ה"א אפי' קטנה, והכתיב "אם אמת וגו'", אלמא דילפינן קנס ממיתה. אלא ודאי, אי לא כתיב "בתולת ישראל", ה"א דאפילו הורתה ולידתה שלא בקדושה הוה מרבינן מ"ומתה", ו"בישראל" אהני שלא ילקה ולא ישלם מאה כסף; אבל השתא דשמעינן לה מ"בתולת ישראל", ע"כ "בישראל" אתא למעוטי הורתה ולידתה שלא בקדושה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:3:1.english: "If so, what purpose does 'in Israel' serve?" - This is puzzling to the Rashba: Let us say it serves [to teach] that he is not lashed and does not pay a hundred silver [shekels]! And Ri says that it is logical that it should apply to everything written in the passage. And furthermore, Ri says that with regard to lashes and the hundred silver [shekels], there is no need to exclude [her] from "in Israel," for we exclude them from "a virgin of Israel" — [meaning] and not a virgin of converts. And now it works out well, so that one will not ask: Why was "a virgin of Israel" — and not a virgin of converts — needed? Derive it from "in Israel"! And even though it is written with regard to the death penalty, nevertheless we derive the fine from it, as is implied shortly below, where [the Gemara] says: "The reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'a young woman'; otherwise, I would have said even a minor — but is it not written 'If [this thing] be true, etc.'!" Thus we see that we derive the fine from the death penalty. Rather, certainly, if "a virgin of Israel" were not written, I would have said that even one whose conception and birth were not in sanctity we would include from "and she shall die," and "in Israel" would serve [to teach] that he is not lashed and does not pay a hundred silver [shekels]; but now that we learn it from "a virgin of Israel," perforce "in Israel" comes to exclude [from the death penalty] one whose conception and birth were not in sanctity.

Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:4:1.hebrew: המוציא שם רע על היתומה פטור כו' - תימה, דתקשי ליה ממתני' דקתני: "הורתה שלא בקדושה ולידתה בקדושה — הרי זו בסקילה, ואין לה פתח בית אב, ולא מאה כסף"; משמע: הא ישראלית גמורה דכוותה שאין לה אב — יש לה מאה כסף! ולעיל נמי תנן דגיורת פחותה מבת ג' יש לה קנס. וי"ל: דמוקי מתני' אליבא דר"ע, דאמר לעיל (כתובות דף לח.): "נערה שנתארסה ונתגרשה — קנסה לעצמה", ודריש: "אשר לא אורסה" — לאביה, הא אורסה — לעצמה; וה"נ דריש: "לאבי הנערה" — הא אין לה אב, לעצמה. אבל ר' יוסי בר' חנינא דהכא — אליבא דר"י הגלילי קאמר דפטור, דכי היכי דדריש לעיל: הא אורסה — אין לה קנס, ה"נ דריש הכא: "לאבי הנערה" — הא אין לה אב, אין לה קנס. ורבא דפליג עליה סבר דאפי' לר"י הגלילי חייב, מדתני אמי דדריש ליה מקרא, ומסתבר דלא פליג שום תנא אההיא דרשא. והשתא פריך הכא רבי יוסי בר אבין מדתני: "אם מאן ימאן" — לרבות יתומה לקנס, דברי ר"י הגלילי. וה"ג ר"ח, וכן במכילתא גרס: "דברי ר' יוסי הגלילי"; ופריך מר' יוסי הגלילי אר' יוסי הגלילי לר' יוסי בר' חנינא. וכן משמע בהדיא בירושלמי, דר' יוסי בר' חנינא אליבא דר' יוסי הגלילי קאמר לה, ומתני' כר"ע; ופריך נמי מ"לרבות יתומה לקנס, דברי ר' יוסי הגלילי", ומשני נמי כדמשני הכא, אבל התם קאמר מילתיה אאונס ואמפתה, ולא אמוציא שם רע:
Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:4:1.english: The defamer of an orphan [girl] is exempt, etc. - This is puzzling, for one could challenge him [Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina] from the Mishnah, which teaches: "[If] her conception was not in sanctity and her birth was in sanctity, she is [executed] by stoning, and she has no 'entrance to her father's house,' nor [the fine of] one hundred silver [shekels]" — implying that a full-fledged Israelite [girl] in her situation, who has no father, does have [the fine of] one hundred silver [shekels]! And earlier as well we learned in a Mishnah that a convert [girl] younger than three years old has a fine. And one can answer: He [Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina] establishes the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who said earlier (Ketubot 38a) [that for] a young woman who was betrothed and divorced, her fine belongs to herself, and he expounds [the verse]: "[who] was not betrothed" — [her fine goes] to her father, [implying that] if she was betrothed, [it goes] to herself. And similarly here, he expounds: "to the father of the young woman" — [implying that] if she has no father, [it goes] to herself. However, Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina here speaks in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, [holding] that he is exempt; for just as he [Rabbi Yosei HaGelili] expounds earlier [that] if she was betrothed, she has no fine, so too here he expounds: "to the father of the young woman" — [implying that] if she has no father, she has no fine. And Rava, who disagrees with him, holds that even according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili he is obligated, based on what Ami taught, who expounds it from a verse — and it stands to reason that no Tanna disagrees with that exposition. And now, Rabbi Yosei bar Avin raises an objection here from what was taught [in a baraita]: "If [her father] utterly refuse [ma'en yima'en]" — to include an orphan for the fine, [these are] the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. And this is how Rabbeinu Ḥananel reads [the text], and so too in the Mekhilta it reads: "[these are] the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili"; and he [Rabbi Yosei bar Avin] raises an objection from [one statement of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili against [another statement of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, according to Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina. And so it is explicitly implied in the [Talmud] Yerushalmi, that Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said this in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, while the Mishnah is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva; and [the Yerushalmi] also raises an objection from "to include an orphan for the fine, [these are] the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili," and it also resolves it as it resolves it here — except that there it states its teaching with regard to a rapist and a seducer, and not with regard to a defamer.

Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:7:1.hebrew: בתולת ישראל ולא בתולת גרים - וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך "אם מאן ימאן" לרבות יתומה? מ"בתולת ישראל" נפקא, מדממעט דווקא בת גרים! ולמאי דפ"ה דיתומה לאו מרבויא משתמעא, ניחא. ונראה לרשב"א, דאי לאו דמרבינן יתומה מ"מאן ימאן", לא הוה דרשינן "בתולת ישראל" ולא בתולת גרים אלא לדרשה אחריתי, כיון דמשום בת גרים לא צריך קרא, דמ"ונתן לאבי הנערה" נפקא, ולא היה סברא לומר דלא איצטריך קרא אלא לדיוקא, הא יתומה בת ישראל יש לה קנס; אבל השתא דמרבינן יתומה, לית לן למעוטי מ"לאבי הנערה" בת גרים, דדרשינן שפיר: "בתולת ישראל" — ולא בתולת גרים:
Tosafot on Ketubot 44b:7:1.english: "A virgin of Israel" — and not a virgin [who is] a convert - And if you ask: Why is [the verse] "if he utterly refuses" [im ma'en yema'en] needed to include an orphan? It is derived from "a virgin of Israel," since [the verse] specifically excludes [only] the daughter of converts! And according to what Rashi explained, that an orphan is not inferred from an inclusionary phrase, this is satisfactory. And it appears to the Rashba that if we did not include an orphan from "he utterly refuses" [ma'en yema'en], we would not expound "a virgin of Israel" — and not a virgin [who is] a convert — except for a different exposition, since for the daughter of converts no verse is needed, as it is derived from "and he shall give to the father of the maiden," and it would not be reasonable to say that the verse was only needed for the inference that an orphan who is a daughter of Israel receives a fine; however, now that we include an orphan, we cannot exclude the daughter of converts from "to the father of the maiden," so we properly expound: "a virgin of Israel" — and not a virgin [who is] a convert.
